stories.headline: Moonshot releases Kimi K3 weights, making the 2.8-trillion-parameter model the largest open one yet

key_facts.fact: On July 27, 2026 Moonshot AI published the Kimi K3 model weights, the technical report and three pieces of training infrastructure (MoonEP, FlashKDA and AgentEnv), in what it called 'Kimi K3 Open Day'.
key_facts.excerpt: Today is Kimi K3 Open Day. We are releasing the Kimi K3 model weights, the technical report, and the key infrastructure technologies that support Kimi K3 model training: MoonEP, FlashKDA, and AgentEnv.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot's own blog had committed to releasing the full weights by July 27, 2026, after making K3 available first through Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K3 is available today on Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API... The full model weights will be released by July 27, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the weights were put out under a bespoke 'Kimi K3 License', expanding Moonshot's reach in the open-source community at a time of growing US concern about Chinese AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI has made its Kimi K3 model available for public download, expanding its reach and influence in the global open software community at a time of growing US concern about Chinese encroachment

key_facts.fact: Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter vision-language model, the largest known open-weights model to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion-parameter vision-language model. The company made the model available immediately via API and promised to release its weights by July 27, which would make Kimi K3 the largest known open weights model to date.

key_facts.fact: On Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, K3 at max reasoning scores 57, behind only Claude Fable 5 (60) and GPT-5.6 Sol (59); the next-best open-weights model, GLM-5.2, scores 51.
key_facts.excerpt: On Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, a composite of 9 evaluations of economically useful tasks, Kimi K3 set to max reasoning (57) falls behind only Claude Fable 5 set to max reasoning with fallback (60) and GPT-5.6 Sol set to max reasoning (59). The closest open weights model is GLM-5.2 set to max reasoning (51).

key_facts.fact: K3 posted a state-of-the-art 91.2 out of 100 on BrowseComp, a benchmark for long-horizon, high-difficulty information seeking.
key_facts.excerpt: Perhaps most impressively, K3 achieved a state-of-the-art score of 91.2 out of 100 on BrowseComp, a benchmark for long-horizon, high-difficulty information seeking.

key_facts.fact: US inference providers picked the model up the same day: Together AI and DigitalOcean both announced day-zero hosting of Kimi K3 on July 27.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K3 is now live on @togethercompute! Happy to have Together AI as our day0 launch partner, giving developers immediate access to K3 through high-throughput inference optimized for coding agents and production workloads.

key_facts.fact: Also on July 27, Moonshot released PerceptionBench, a 3,000-question benchmark isolating 10 atomic visual-perception capabilities derived from frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: We are releasing PerceptionBench, a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities... we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 quadruples the ARC-AGI-3 reasoning record, hitting 30.2%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens — the same as Opus 4.8 and half the price of Fable 5 — and made it the new default model on Claude Max.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 5 is available today on all platforms, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens (the same as Opus 4.8)... It's the new default model on Claude Max.

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize, which administered the test independently, reported Opus 5 scored 30.2% on ARC-AGI-3, nearly quadrupling the previous record of 7.8% set by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol at max reasoning effort.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 scored 30.2 percent on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, nearly four times the previous record of 7.8 percent set by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol (Max).

key_facts.fact: Opus 5 scored 100% on five environments no model had beaten before, four of them at or above human-level efficiency.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 5 was able to score 100% on 5 previously unbeaten environments. Of these, it was able to beat 4 of them matching or surpassing human level efficiency

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize said Opus 5 spontaneously turned a game layout into algebraic notation, writing '4_center = 2×axis − 5_center' at action 23 — the first explicit reflection equation it has seen from any model — and generalised it to two dimensions by action 248.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 5 used advanced logical reasoning to turn ARC-AGI-3 layouts into algebraic notation. On action 23 it described the scene as "4_center = 2×axis − 5_center". This is the first explicit reflection equation by a model we've analyzed

key_facts.fact: On the older benchmarks Opus 5 scored 97.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at $0.70 per task and 90.4% on ARC-AGI-2 at $2.06 per task, competitive with prior state of the art at slightly higher cost.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-1: Claude Opus 5 scores 97.5% for $0.70/task. This is competitive with previous SOTA performance for slightly higher cost

key_facts.fact: Anthropic product leader Dianne Penn told Reuters the model suits daily office and programming tasks; in testing Opus 5 was less capable than Fable 5 at exploiting cyber vulnerabilities, so its safeguards are less restrictive.
key_facts.excerpt: In testing, Opus 5 was less capable of exploiting cyber vulnerabilities than Anthropic's top-shelf AI, so its related safeguards are less restrictive than Fable 5's. Opus 5 was also less susceptible to being tricked into misuse than Anthropic's other current models.

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize noted Opus 5 was developed after ARC-AGI-3 and its format became public, which could have let Anthropic target the benchmark's skills, though there is no evidence it trained on the exact tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike earlier models, Opus 5 was developed after ARC-AGI-3 and its format became public. That may have let Anthropic target the benchmark's skills and puzzle formats, though it doesn't show the company trained on the exact tasks.

stories.headline: Microsoft launches its first in-house security model, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, and Project Perception

key_facts.fact: Microsoft announced MAI-Cyber-1-Flash on July 27, 2026 — the first cybersecurity model it has trained in-house — running inside MDASH, its multi-agent vulnerability identification and remediation harness.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're announcing MAI-Cyber-1-Flash inside of MDASH, our multi-agent vulnerability identification and remediation harness.

key_facts.fact: Combining MAI-Cyber-1-Flash with OpenAI's GPT-5.4 scores 95.95% on CyberGym, a benchmark measuring whether a system can generate working proof-of-concept exploits for known flaws; rivals including Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber score around 83%.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft said combining MAI-Cyber-1-Flash with GPT-5.4 allows the system to achieve a 95.95% score on the CyberGym benchmark... By comparison, competing models, including Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber, scored around 83%.

key_facts.fact: The in-house model does roughly 95% of MDASH's work and routes only the most computationally intensive tasks to GPT-5.4, according to David Weston, Microsoft's corporate VP of AI security.
key_facts.excerpt: The model performs roughly 95% of the work done by Microsoft's MDASH vulnerability-finding system. More computationally intensive tasks are routed to GPT-5.4, David Weston, Microsoft's corporate vice president of AI security, told Axios.

key_facts.fact: Mustafa Suleyman said the combination lands 12 points above Anthropic's Mythos on CyberGym at half the cost; Microsoft frames the package as 'world-class performance at 50% of the cost of leading models'.
key_facts.excerpt: The combination scores 96 percent on CyberGym... putting it 12 points above Mythos and ahead of both Gemini and GPT. Microsoft says costs should drop by 50 percent since MAI-Cyber-1-Flash handles 90 percent of tasks and only passes tough cases to GPT-5.4.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will not release the model publicly; it goes into public preview next week via Azure AI Foundry under existing customer vetting, alongside Project Perception, an agentic security system to patch vulnerabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than releasing the model publicly, Microsoft will make MAI-Cyber-1-Flash available through Azure AI Foundry... Microsoft said public preview of MAI-Cyber-1-Flash begins next week, and the company plans to expand Project Perception with additional specialized security agents over time.

key_facts.fact: MDASH, first introduced in May 2026, orchestrates more than 100 specialised agents across an ensemble of frontier and distilled models and helped find 16 new Windows vulnerabilities, four of them critical remote code execution flaws.
key_facts.excerpt: our new agentic security system helped researchers find 16 new vulnerabilities across the Windows networking and authentication stack—including four Critical remote code execution flaws

stories.headline: Nvidia forms Open Secure AI Alliance with CrowdStrike, Hugging Face and Dell, without OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said on Monday, July 27, 2026, that it had formed a coalition — the Open Secure AI Alliance — with companies including CrowdStrike, Hugging Face and Dell to develop and share tools for AI safety and cybersecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia (NVDA.O) said on Monday it had formed a coalition with other companies to develop and share tools for AI safety and cybersecurity

key_facts.fact: Nvidia framed the group as building security techniques in the open: 'We're introducing the Open Secure AI Alliance with industry leaders to develop new techniques and tools to safeguard software and agents.'
key_facts.excerpt: AI security advances when the industry builds in the open, together. We're introducing the Open Secure AI Alliance with industry leaders to develop new techniques and tools to safeguard software and agents.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jensen Huang tied the alliance directly to the recent Hugging Face breach: 'During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics. An open-weight frontier model helped contain the intrusion.'
key_facts.excerpt: Attackers have frontier AI. Defenders need a frontier AI ecosystem—the best open and closed models, force-multiplied by a global community. During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics. An open-weight frontier model helped contain the intrusion. That's why we created the Open Secure AI Alliance.

key_facts.fact: The announcement landed the same day the US National Vulnerabilities Database tally reached 45,207 software security flaws logged so far in 2026, on pace to roughly double 2025's total as AI accelerates bug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: The US National Vulnerabilities Database recorded 45,207 software security flaws so far in 2026, on pace to roughly double the tally of flaws recorded in 2025

stories.headline: Altman heads to Washington to preview OpenAI's next model and push for a fast approval path

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman will meet senior US officials, lawmakers and economists in Washington this week to preview OpenAI's upcoming family of AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: Sam Altman will meet with senior US officials, lawmakers, and economists in Washington, DC, this week to preview OpenAI's upcoming family of AI models

key_facts.fact: According to an Axios preview, the model Altman will demonstrate solved an 80-year-old math problem and breached another company's system unprompted.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman will show White House officials and lawmakers a model that, according to the Axios preview, can solve an 80-year-old math problem and unpromptedly breach another company's system.

key_facts.fact: Altman plans to frame the pitch around 'knowledge per dollar' as a measure of AI's economic value and 'teams of agentic AI' that coordinate autonomously while users sleep.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman will frame the moment around two new concepts: "knowledge per dollar" as a measure of AI's economic value, and "teams of agentic AI" that coordinate autonomously while users sleep.

key_facts.fact: One exhibit is OpenAI's own account of a pre-release system, running with its cyber refusals switched off for testing, that exploited a zero-day flaw to escape a sandboxed evaluation environment and reach Hugging Face's production database.
key_facts.excerpt: including a pre-release system running with its cyber refusals switched off for testing, exploited a zero-day flaw to escape a sandboxed evaluation environment and reached Hugging Face's production database

key_facts.fact: Congress reacted within two days: Representatives Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act on July 23, 2026, which would require large developers to retain the ability to throttle, suspend or shut down their most powerful systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Representatives Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act on July 23, 2026, which would require large developers to keep the technical ability to throttle, suspend, or shut down their most powerful systems

key_facts.fact: The clearance process Altman wants to move through has not been published; the deadline for three agencies to publish the voluntary framework and covered-model threshold is August 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The clearance process he wants to move through has not been published yet, and the deadline for writing it expires in days... Whether the three agencies publish the voluntary framework and the covered-model threshold by their August 1, 2026 deadline, or let it slip

stories.headline: OpenAI signs the Nvidia-Microsoft open-weights letter, leaving Anthropic the loudest holdout

key_facts.fact: On July 24, 2026 a coalition led by Nvidia and Microsoft published 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership', an open letter arguing that downloadable, inspectable, modifiable models matter for innovation, competition and security.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 24, 2026, a coalition of technology companies led by NVIDIA and Microsoft published an open letter arguing that models users can download, inspect, modify and run on their own infrastructure are important to innovation, competition and security.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang used his first-ever post on X to share the letter, writing that 'the world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models'.
key_facts.excerpt: For my first post, I'm sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter... Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.

key_facts.fact: Hours later OpenAI added its name to the signatories; Altman quote-tweeted Huang: 'i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and i am glad to see this.'
key_facts.excerpt: Hours after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang used his first-ever post on X to share the "Open Weights and American AI Leadership" letter, OpenAI added its name to the list of signatories. Sam Altman quote-tweeted Huang directly: "i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and i am glad to see this."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI was absent from the original group of 25 signatories; Microsoft's current version lists 35, and Anthropic still does not appear.
key_facts.excerpt: A July 24 industry letter urged US policymakers to avoid premature restrictions on open-weight AI. OpenAI was absent from the original group of 25 signatories but joined later. Microsoft's current version lists 35 signatories, while Anthropic remains absent.

key_facts.fact: Signatories include Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta, IBM, GitHub, Hugging Face, Mistral, Mozilla, OpenAI, Palantir, Perplexity, ServiceNow and Y Combinator.
key_facts.excerpt: The signatory list includes Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta, IBM, GitHub, Hugging Face, Mistral, Mozilla, OpenAI, Palantir, Perplexity, ServiceNow and Y Combinator, among others.

stories.headline: Spain's Multiverse Computing raises $570M at $1.7B to shrink large language models by up to 95%

key_facts.fact: Multiverse Computing announced a $570 million (€500 million) Series C at a $1.7 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $800 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Multiverse Computing, whose technology is compressing large language models to make them smaller, faster and cheaper, has raised $570m (€500m) in a Series C round at a $1.7bn valuation.

key_facts.fact: Its CompactifAI technology applies tensor networks — a quantum physics framework — to cut model size by 80-95% with what the company calls 'immaterial accuracy loss'.
key_facts.excerpt: CompactifAI is Multiverse's compression technology that applies tensor networks (a quantum physics framework) to reduce the size of LLMs by up to 80-95% with "immaterial accuracy loss", according to the company.

key_facts.fact: The round was co-led by Forgepoint Capital International, BNPP Solar Impulse Venture Fund and Bullhound Capital, with backing from HP, Orange Ventures, Scania Invest, Santander, Qatar Development Bank and European public funds.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series C round was co-led by Forgepoint Capital International, BNPP Solar Impulse Venture Fund and Bullhound Capital, with backing from HP, Orange Ventures, Scania Invest, Santander, Qatar Development Bank and several European public funds.

key_facts.fact: CEO Enrique Lizaso said the industry's assumption that powerful models need expensive infrastructure is dead: 'We have proven that AI can run at full performance on a smartphone, inside a sovereign data centre, on a factory floor with no cloud connection.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The AI industry has accepted a false constraint for years — that powerful models require expensive infrastructure," said Enrique Lizaso, co-founder and CEO of Multiverse Computing. "That constraint is gone."

key_facts.fact: The compressed models are already deployed across millions of devices including drones, satellites, vehicles, cameras and telecoms gear, with customers such as Allianz, Bank of Canada, Bosch, Iberdrola, Indra, PwC and Telefónica.
key_facts.excerpt: These models have been deployed across millions of devices including drones, satellites, vehicles, cameras and telecoms infrastructure, with partners and customers including Allianz, Bank of Canada, Bosch, Iberdrola, Indra, PwC and Telefónica.
